newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco B falls, traders say govt selling.
newsitem.headline: Meralco B falls, traders say govt selling.

text.p: Manila Electric Co B shares slipped at midsession on Friday amid talk of foreign selling and a government institution selling its B shares, traders said.
Diversified Securities executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said that two foreign brokerage houses were actively selling Meralco's B shares.
Another trader said a government institution was selling its holdings.
"One of the government agencies with Meralco B holdings is selling its shares," the trader, who asked not to be identified, said.
Meralco B shares shed one peso to 128 pesos in midtrade.
Meralco B were sold down on Thursday, closing sharply lower by 13 pesos, or 9.15 percent, to 129 pesos on what traders said was due to foreign selling.
Meralco spokesman Elpi Cuna said the firm had no knowledge of a government institution selling its B shares.
Officials at the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG), which holds Meralco shares, were not immediately available for comment.
PCGG, the custodian of all sequestered assets of the late Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates, holds about 30 percent of Meralco.
Other government financial institutions with holdings in Meralco include the Social Security System and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS).
